_comment: 図ソース台帳（SSOT）。資格(category slug)ごとに、記事図クロップの元素材の所在・種別・品質・再スキャン要否を1度記録する。build-figure-provenance.mjs が図の provenance を組むときに参照。図の実ソースを毎回手で辿らないための恒久記録。更新: content/sources/textbook 実体 + 図品質監査(sharpness) を根拠に随時。

_fields.source_dir: 元素材のディレクトリ（content/sources/textbook 配下）
_fields.source_kind: pdf-vector(図がPDFにベクター/画像で入る) | pdf-textonly(問題PDFは図なしテキスト版) | scan-image(書籍スキャンpngのみ・PDF無し) | mixed
_fields.figure_origin: 記事図クロップの実際の出所（question-pdf / answer-booklet / textbook-scan / ai-generated / unknown）
_fields.quality: print-clean(印刷/デジタル・鮮明) | scan-low(書籍スキャン・低品質) | mixed
_fields.rescannable: true=元書籍/資料を高解像度再スキャンで品質改善可 / needs-source=元資料の入手が要 / na

_manual_needs_comment: 機械監査(OCR/sharpness)では検出不能な図欠陥の per-figure 上書き。特に『元図が上下で見切れて図要素/答えが欠落』は鮮明かつ写り込み無し=textStatus:clean のため needs:ok と誤判定される。build-figure-provenance.mjs が baseRel 末尾一致で needs を上書きする。figure=baseRel 末尾（slug/img/名）。

civil-construction-1/textbook-coast-port.prompt: A floating crane vessel (crane barge) at a port: a large flat steel barge with a tall fixed A-frame or fixed-boom heavy-lift crane at one end, heavy wire ropes and a big lifting block lifting a huge rectangular reinforced-concrete caisson (a box-shaped concrete block with open top and internal cells, light grey, several meters wide) a short distance above the water surface, lowering it towards a prepared breakwater foundation. Tugboats nearby, calm sea, breakwater construction site in background. Seen from a slight angle at eye level above the water, shallow depth of field.

A grab dredger working at a port: a flat-deck steel barge (pontoon) carrying a large revolving crane with a lattice boom; from the boom a clamshell grab bucket hangs on wire ropes, partly opened just above the water surface, muddy water around it. Calm sea, a small tugboat and a mud-hauling barge visible in the distance. Seen from a slight angle at eye level above the water, shallow depth of field.

A land reclamation construction site at the sea: a sea area enclosed by a perimeter seawall revetment (rock and concrete embankment) forming a reclamation basin. In the foreground, a large-diameter steel discharge pipe (slurry pipeline) runs along the top of the embankment and its open end discharges a strong jet of muddy sand-and-water mixture into the enclosed basin, forming a brown fan of sediment and a sandy beach-like slope. Beyond, the enclosing revetment and open sea behind it, with a spillway outlet structure at the far edge. Slightly elevated viewpoint, shallow depth of field, no people.

A sand compaction pile (SCP) vessel at sea: a large flat steel work barge carrying several tall vertical lattice-steel leader towers (very tall, like pile-driver masts, higher than any superstructure), each with a vibratory hammer unit mounted at the upper part of the mast and a long vertical steel casing pipe running down the mast and into the water. A sand hopper and a cabin on the deck, anchor wires leading to the sea. The vessel is stationary, casing pipes lowered into the seabed. Calm sea, hazy distant shoreline, seen from a slight angle at eye level above the water, shallow depth of field.

A composite breakwater whose sea-side front is covered by a thick armor layer of wave-dissipating concrete blocks (grey four-legged tetrapod-type interlocking blocks piled in a sloping mass, in several layers, reaching nearly to the top). Behind and slightly above the blocks, the flat top of a concrete caisson superstructure (parapet crest) is visible running along the breakwater. Viewed from the sea side at a low angle along the breakwater, waves breaking gently on the blocks, calm weather, shallow depth of field.

civil-construction-1/textbook-crane/img/.prompt: An all-terrain crane (large mobile crane): a multi-axle wheeled carrier with 5 axles and 10 large road tires, a separate driver's cab at the front of the carrier and a separate crane operator's cab on the rotating superstructure, a telescopic box-section boom partly extended, four outriggers extended onto pads, counterweight at the rear.

A telescopic-boom aerial work platform truck: a light truck with a straight telescopic boom extended upward at an angle, a work platform (basket) with guardrails at the boom tip next to a street lighting pole, outriggers extended. One worker in the basket wearing a helmet and harness, small and seen from a distance, face not visible.

A cable crane at a large concrete dam construction site in a mountain valley: steel towers on both sides of the valley with main track wire ropes spanned across the valley between them, a carriage (trolley) running on the cables with a large concrete bucket hanging from hoist ropes, the dam body under construction below. Wide view.

A crawler crane: full-hydraulic machine on two long steel crawler track frames, a rotating upper structure with operator cab and rear counterweight, a long LATTICE-structure boom (open steel truss) raised at about 60 degrees with hoist wire ropes, pendant lines and a hook block hanging from the boom tip. Unpaved soil ground.

A truck-mounted loader crane (about 3 t class cargo crane truck): an ordinary flatbed cargo truck with a small hydraulic telescopic straight-boom crane mounted BETWEEN the truck cab and the cargo bed, small outriggers extended, the boom lifting a bundle of steel pipes with slings onto the bed.

A rough-terrain crane: a short two-axle carrier with four large off-road tires of equal size, a SINGLE cab on the rotating upper structure (one operator both drives and operates the crane), a telescopic box-section boom, four outriggers extended with floats on the ground, on an unpaved site.

A climbing tower crane on a high-rise building under construction: a lattice steel tower mast standing inside / attached to the building frame, a horizontal lattice jib with a trolley and hook, a counter-jib with concrete counterweight blocks and the operator cab at the top. Viewed from ground level at a distance so the whole crane is in frame.

civil-construction-1/textbook-distance-a.prompt: A surveying reflector prism on a prism pole for electronic distance measurement: a round glass corner-cube prism in a holder with a target plate, mounted on top of a red-and-white graduated prism pole with a small circular bubble level, the pole held vertical by a bipod over a survey point. Frame from the prism down to mid-pole.

A GNSS (satellite positioning) surveying receiver set up on a tripod: a white dome-shaped GNSS antenna/receiver unit on a tribrach on top of a surveying tripod, with a small handheld data controller clipped to a tripod leg, under clear open sky on a construction site.

A surveying total station on a wooden tripod with three legs, set up on dry compacted soil at a civil construction site, side view. A large round dark grey surveyor's umbrella with a smooth flat underside is held by a straight metal pole planted in the ground on the far side behind the tripod, tilted slightly so the canopy extends over the instrument, with a clear empty gap of air between the canopy and the top of the instrument. The underside of the canopy is plain fabric with ribs only; nothing hangs down from the canopy, no spike, no rod, no tip under the canopy, and the canopy does not touch the instrument. The instrument and the tripod head sit inside the cool soft shadow of the canopy, clearly darker than the sunlit ground around them, while the ground outside the shadow is bright. Shallow depth of field, blurred construction site background. No text, no logos, no people.

A modern electronic theodolite (digital transit) mounted on a yellow aluminium surveying tripod. It must look like a real contemporary electronic theodolite: a telescope (with objective lens) held between two vertical standards (a U-shaped alidade), a small LCD keypad display on the alidade face, a horizontal circle housing below, a tribrach with three leveling screws seated on the tripod head, and a vertical clamp/tangent knob on the standard. The whole instrument and the top half of the tripod legs are visible.

A modern total station on a surveying tripod: a telescope with built-in electronic distance meter between two standards, a carrying handle on top, LCD displays with keypads on both faces of the alidade, a tribrach with three leveling screws, on a yellow tripod at a construction site.

civil-construction-1/textbook-grader-com.prompt: A macadam road roller - a three-wheel static steel roller with a FIXED (rigid) frame: ONE wide steel drum at the front used for steering, and TWO large-diameter steel drive rolls at the rear, one on each side, operator seat between them, compacting a crushed-stone base course of a road.

A motor grader: a long-wheelbase frame with a long blade (moldboard) mounted under the MIDDLE of the frame between the front and rear axles, a single front axle with two tires, rear TANDEM axles with four tires, the cab at the rear above the engine, grading a gravel road.
A sheepsfoot tamping roller (soil compactor): a self-propelled compactor whose front steel drum is covered with many protruding sheep's-foot pads (rod-like feet), compacting a clay embankment fill.

A two-axle static tandem road roller: two SMOOTH steel drums of nearly the same width and diameter, one at the front and one at the rear, operator platform in the middle, finishing a freshly laid asphalt pavement.

A pneumatic tire roller: a compactor with a row of smooth rubber tires at the front (4 tires) and a row at the rear (5 tires) staggered so their tracks overlap, a box-shaped ballast body, operator seat with canopy on top, compacting asphalt pavement.

civil-construction-1/textbook-leveling/i.prompt: An automatic level (auto level) for surveying on a tripod: a compact horizontal telescope body with objective lens and eyepiece, a focusing knob, a circular bubble level, three leveling screws on the base plate, mounted on an aluminium tripod; a levelling staff stands in the soft-focus background.

civil-construction-1/textbook-loader/img.prompt: A wheel loader: articulated frame, four large tires of equal size, a front bucket on lift arms, the cab in the middle and engine at the rear, loading gravel from a stockpile.

civil-construction-1/textbook-safety-exc.prompt: Construction site photo of a slab formwork shoring system built with adjustable steel pipe supports (pipe props, painted orange-red, with pin-adjusted telescoping tubes) standing vertically under plywood formwork. Each prop base sits on a timber sleeper plank (shikikaku) laid on the compacted ground. Horizontal bracing tubes (steel pipes) run in two perpendicular directions, X and Y, between the props at roughly every 2 m height, crossing each other and fastened to the props with bolted steel coupler clamps; the splice joint between two prop sections is also secured with a bolted metal fitting. Shallow depth of field, focus on the crossing of the horizontal braces and the bolted coupler joint, background softly blurred. No people, no faces, no text, no logos.

civil-construction-1/textbook-safety-fou.prompt: A crawler-type pile driver (full-swing crawler rig with a tall vertical leader mast standing plumb) positioned on a work platform made of large rectangular steel plates (shikitetsuban) laid side by side on compacted ground at a civil engineering construction site. Two tension guy cables (back-stay wires) run from the top of the leader down diagonally to the rear of the machine body, anchored near the rear. The mast is perfectly vertical, the steel plates are flat and tightly aligned with visible bolt-lug edges and slight dust, crawler tracks fully resting on the plates. Shallow depth of field, side three-quarter view from a low angle, overcast daylight, no people, no text, no logos, no signage.

civil-construction-1/textbook-safety-sca.prompt: Side view of a steel frame scaffold (wakugumi ashiba) on a construction site, photographed from a slight diagonal angle. Vertical steel frames (tatewaku) stacked in tiers, X-shaped cross braces (kosa sujikai) between adjacent frames, and a horizontal lower rail (shitazan) bar at low height above the work deck, plus a toe board. Galvanized steel, grey tone, working platforms with planks. Shallow depth of field, soft overcast light. No people, no text, no logos.

Close-up macro photograph of two steel wire ropes lying on a concrete floor at a construction site. One rope has several broken outer strands, with frayed, splayed wire ends sticking out (broken wires, birdcaging). The other rope has a kink, a sharp permanent bend with the strands distorted and flattened at the fold. Galvanized steel, slightly rusty and oily. Very shallow depth of field, soft natural light. No people, no text, no logos, no tags.

civil-construction-1/textbook-safety-wor.prompt: Back view of a construction worker from the neck down to the knees standing on a civil engineering site, face not visible, head turned away and cropped at the top of the frame. Wearing a white industrial safety helmet with an inner shock-absorbing liner and chin strap seen from behind, a full-body safety harness with shoulder straps and a back D-ring, a disposable-style dust mask hanging visible at the side of the neck, orange high-visibility vest, work gloves. Plain blurred earthwork site background with shallow depth of field. No text, no logos, no readable markings.

civil-construction-1/textbook-scraper/im.prompt: A self-propelled wheeled motor scraper with two axles in total: a single-axle tractor unit at the front carrying the cab and engine, connected by a gooseneck to a rear scraper bowl unit on its own axle, with the apron, cutting edge and ejector visible, large earthmover tires, cutting and loading soil while moving at an earthworks site.

A scrape dozer - a Japanese crawler-type earthmoving machine that combines a scraper and a bulldozer. Two CONTINUOUS steel crawler tracks run the full length of the machine on the left and right sides, unbroken from front idler to rear sprocket. A large open scraper BOWL loaded with soil sits in the MIDDLE of the machine, BETWEEN the left and right tracks, where an ordinary bulldozer would have its engine. A straight dozer blade is mounted at the front. The engine compartment with a radiator grille is at the REAR. The operator seat is on a raised platform above the bowl and faces SIDEWAYS (perpendicular to the direction of travel), with hydraulic control levers in front of the seat under a simple canopy. Spreading soil on soft ground. Side view from slightly above so that the full-length track and the bowl between the tracks are both visible.

civil-construction-1/textbook-soft-groun.prompt: A residential street in a Japanese suburban neighborhood right after an earthquake, asphalt road surface with several cracks from which wet gray silty sand and muddy water has welled up and spread in irregular patches and small mounds on the pavement, a side gutter partially filled with gray sand, low concrete block wall and plain houses blurred in the background, overcast daylight, wet sand texture in sharp focus, shallow depth of field, no people, no signs or text

civil-construction-1/textbook-steel-stru.prompt: Realistic documentary photograph of the end of a highway steel plate girder bridge seen from the side at abutment level, shallow depth of field. A concrete abutment (bridge seat) top supports a rectangular rubber bearing pad (elastomeric bearing) on a steel sole plate; the bottom flange of the steel I-girder rests directly on top of the bearing. Behind the girder end, a vertical concrete parapet wall (breast wall) rises, with a narrow expansion gap between the girder end and the parapet wall, and a steel finger-type expansion joint device visible at the deck level above. Gray concrete, slightly weathered gray-painted steel, overcast daylight, no people, no text, no logos.

civil-construction-1/textbook-tractor-bu.prompt: A medium-size crawler bulldozer (15 to 21 t class): steel crawler tracks, a straight dozer blade at the front, a single-shank ripper at the rear, a cab with ROPS, pushing soil at an earthworks site.

civil-construction-1/textbook-transport-.prompt: A portable belt conveyor: a short wheeled conveyor frame inclined at about 20 degrees, a rubber belt carrying sand and gravel, a small electric motor at the head pulley, discharging onto a pile at a small construction site.

An articulated dump truck: a front tractor unit with the cab and one axle, an articulation (hinge) joint behind the cab, and a rear dump body on TWO axles - six large off-road tires in total - hauling earth on a rough haul road at an earthworks site.

Close-up photograph of a belt conveyor side frame at an aggregate or gravel plant. A steel wire pull-cord emergency stop rope runs horizontally along the side of the conveyor frame at hand height beside the running belt, held by small eye bolts at regular intervals, with a rectangular pull-cord switch box mounted on the frame at one end of the rope. Next to it, a yellow-background emergency stop pushbutton with a large red mushroom head mounted on a steel post on the conveyor frame. Painted steel frame, idler rollers and the belt edge softly blurred in the background, shallow depth of field, daylight, industrial outdoor setting. No text, no logos, no people, no faces.

A rubber-track crawler carrier (rough-terrain dumper): rubber crawler tracks, a small operator cab at the front and a rear tipping dump bed carrying soil, on muddy uneven ground at a construction site.

civil-construction-1/textbook-water-sewe.prompt: Oblique aerial view from a high vantage point of a municipal sewage treatment plant: a rectangular concrete aeration (reaction) tank full of brown activated sludge with vigorous white foam and bubbling from diffused aeration, running alongside a large circular final settling clarifier with clear water surface and a thin rotating scraper bridge across it, concrete walkways with plain pipe handrails, no buildings with signage, daytime overcast light, shallow depth of field with distant plant blurred

civil-construction-2/guide-road-pavement.prompt: Close-up photo of a roadside drainage gutter along the edge of an asphalt road. A concrete U-shaped gutter runs along the road edge, and its top is covered by a row of rectangular galvanized steel gratings (grid-pattern cover plates with parallel flat bars) fitted flush with the pavement surface, one after another. Rainwater from the wet asphalt surface flows along the road edge toward the gutter and drains through the grating slots.
